newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast crude prices ease as July talk picks up.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast crude prices ease as July talk picks up.

text.p: U.S. West Coast oil prices fell Wednesday under pressure from a lower domestic crude market and concerns of rising supplies.

Crude oil futures for July delivery dropped 21 cents a barrel after the American Petroleum Petroleum reported late Tuesday that crude inventories rose a sharp 8.4 million barrels last week, despite refineries turning large volumes of crude into product.
Although no one sold West Coast crude Wednesday, traders began to discuss July shipments.
Tosco Corp, normally a buyer, was looking to sell a full cargo of regional benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) Wednesday at $2.00 under WTI.
Traders said Texaco was hoping to buy the cargo at $2.25 a barrel for its Anacortes, Wash., refinery.
Buyers expect the next cargo to sell at wider than $2.00 off July WTI.
With Tosco cutting runs of crude oil the last two weeks, the company's refineries have held off using an ANS cargo, and a full cargo of Cano Limon.
Tosco is also offering the Cano Limon, which it bought for $3.10 a barrel under June WTI from Ecopetrol last month, traders said.
ANS outright prices eased five cents a barrel on the day in line with WTI.
Ultramar will bring in cargoes of Oriente crude for July, traders said.
